original_test_intent: Demonstrate that the owner-approved tray can be removed and reinserted while its chassis is operating without physical damage and then successfully boot or rejoin service.
original_method: A qualified operator isolates the selected tray/workload, follows the exact live-service latch and connector sequence, captures the removal/reinsertion and mechanical inspection, then verifies clean tray boot/rejoin and chassis health.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must physically remove and reinsert the exact powered tray, inspect latches/connectors for damage and supervise recovery; the agent cannot perform or attest to those actions.
required_inputs: Exact chassis and tray slot/serial/role plus validated powered-hot-swap capability
Approved latch, disconnect, dwell, reconnect, seat and power sequence
Main/standby/redundancy topology and expected effect on the rest of the chassis
Workload, storage, network and cluster drain/restore authorization
ESD/PPE, safe-access, arc/damage stop criteria and physical inspection checklist
Expected boot/rejoin deadlines, health criteria and independent recovery plan
safety_requirements: Do not remove a powered tray unless the exact platform revision is approved for that live service action
Drain or isolate affected workloads and preserve data/network redundancy first
Use qualified personnel, ESD/PPE and the approved connector/latch order
Stop immediately on arc, heat, odor, resistance, connector damage, unexpected shutdown or redundancy loss
Do not reseat or repeat after an ambiguous mechanical state
Keep workloads isolated until physical integrity and full health are confirmed
agent_execution_scope: Verify identity, approved procedure, workload isolation and recovery readiness
Collect read-only pre/post chassis, BMC, OS, PCIe, storage, network and cluster evidence
Correlate operator physical timestamps with removal, presence and rejoin state
Package evidence and discrepancies without operating hardware
Make no damage observation claim, automatic retry or PASS/FAIL verdict
engineer_actions: Approve that the exact tray/platform supports the powered hot-swap sequence
Provide qualified operator, workload authorization and physical damage evidence
Review recovery and complete health evidence and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: No software command can execute or validate the defining physical unplug/replug and connector-damage inspection; the NO assessment is correct.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only read-only telemetry collection as corroboration around the qualified operator's approved physical sequence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Powered unplug/replug, no-damage and successful post-swap boot requirements plus Manual Validation and 20/20-minute estimates remain.

modernized_recommendation.status: MANUAL ONLY CRITICAL LIVE POWERED-TRAY SERVICE
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute one approved tray/slot sequence with synchronized physical video, connector/latch inspection and complete before/absence/reinsert/boot/rejoin health evidence under independent recovery coverage.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Defines the exact platform support, impact isolation, mechanical acceptance and post-rejoin evidence needed to make the broad source claim auditable.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: BMC or OS reachability after reinsertion cannot prove there was no arcing, bent contact, partial latch or latent connector damage; direct physical inspection remains mandatory.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Removing the wrong tray or a non-hot-swappable powered connector can damage hardware and interrupt chassis services. A successful boot alone also does not prove storage/PCIe/cluster integrity or absence of latent faults.

project_override_considerations: Any model-specific tool, interlock, latch order, standby state or service restriction must come from the approved platform revision; generic server hot-swap assumptions are prohibited.
expected_evidence: Approved platform/tray/slot/serial/topology, live-service procedure and workload authorization
Timestamped baseline, physical removal, absence state, connector/latch inspection and reinsertion video/photos
Tray boot/rejoin timeline and read-only BMC/OS/PCIe/storage/network/cluster comparison
No arc/damage/fault plus normal power/thermal/redundancy restoration

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently describe a powered physical tray hot-swap followed by damage and boot verification. Missing topology and service detail are execution-readiness gaps rather than conflicting meanings.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The agent cannot execute the physical destructive action, but a qualified operator may do so after platform approval; therefore MANUAL ONLY is the correct classification rather than a global BLOCKED status.

review_improvement: Retains MANUAL ONLY and the live-hot-swap coverage while adding exact tray identity, platform authorization, impact isolation, mechanical acceptance and full recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: A tray that boots after reinsertion may still have been placed in a degraded electrical or mechanical state: a partially seated high-current connector can pass initial enumeration yet overheat later, and PCIe/storage/cluster paths may be missing despite an OS prompt. The test therefore needs both direct connector/latch inspection and a multi-domain rejoin comparison. Because the stimulus crosses live power, any ambiguous insertion state must stop the run rather than trigger a second attempt.
